title: Can I BEAT Circular Chess?
summary: Circular Chess on 'Deckmate' (beta web game by solo dev Greenlemon Games). He plays white vs the experimental Circular Chess Bot at level 1 (level 2 recommended). Board is an annulus (ring with a hole); files a-t, ranks wrap around the circle, diagonals stop at sharp sector breaks; each side gets extra knights positioned closer to the enemy. The level-1 bot pushes pawns then sacrifices a rook with a strong tactic; he escapes with a draw by threefold repetition.
rules: Board: ring-shaped (annulus) with files lettered a through t (20 radial sectors - inferred from file letters) and concentric rings as ranks (~8 rings in thumbnail); there is a hole in the middle.
Ranks run 'side to side' and come full circle (a rook can travel all the way around the ring).
Diagonals follow same-coloured squares but END at the sharp sector intersections (no bouncing/continuing past breaks).
Each side has extra knights placed nearer to the enemy (because the board is so big).
White and black armies sit on opposite arcs of the outer rings (white at top, black at bottom in thumbnail), back rank on the outermost ring, pawns one ring in.
Castling exists (he castles). Normal checkmate/draw rules (threefold repetition).
win_condition: Checkmate the bot (video result: draw by threefold repetition vs level 1).
